Fourteen call sites invoked `DataTable({...})` as a plain function rather than as an element, which returns the component's output instead of an element of the component: React never sees `DataTable` as a component, it loses its identity in the tree, and the first time `DataTable` uses a hook the call registers that hook against the _parent_, producing an "Invalid hook call" that points nowhere near the cause. It only worked because `DataTable` happens to be hook-free today — luck, not a property — and the other three table surfaces already used the correct form, so the codebase was half one convention and half another. All fourteen now render `React.createElement<DataTableProps<T>>(DataTable, {...})`; the explicit type argument is required, because without it the row type erases to `unknown` and every `keyExtractor` and column callback silently loses its parameter type. Separately, the record transition history was a stack of `div`s: a record's transitions are an ordered sequence but nothing in the markup said so, so it is now an ordered list named by its own heading, with the box and divider rules as decoration on top of that structure rather than the only structure it had. A guard now fails if any feature calls an imported component as a plain function; it only considers names the file actually imports, so a capitalised platform global such as `URLSearchParams` is not mistaken for a component, and it reads multi-line imports, which is how most views import `DataTable`;
- every guard added in this pass was checked against a scratch violation rather than trusted on a green run, and two of them were wrong first. The empty-state guard passed on a scratch violation; the component-call guard missed a `URLSearchParams({...})` false positive until it was scoped to imported names, then missed the real case — a plain `DataTable({...})` in a file that imports it across several lines — until the import scan was rewritten to read the whole file, and was finally rejected by lint for a regex it could not prove safe, which is why it is a direct character scan. A test that cannot fail is not evidence;
- the select chevron was the last raw SVG outside the icon set and was hand-set to `strokeWidth: 2.5` where the whole set uses 2, making it the one visibly heavier mark in the product; it is now `chevronDown` in the set. 12px is kept deliberately because it is sized to the 34px control rather than to a product icon, and that is now recorded in a comment so it is not "corrected" later. Verified in the browser that every chevron on every route reports 2px and that the empty-state mark measures 8.00:1 against its composited background;
- Runtime still has not been restarted, so the `rolePermissions.mcp`/`skills` projection is verified by the Control API suite and an isolated Console instance pointed at a real execution-contract projection, not against the currently running router. Against the still-running Router, Permissions fails closed with `autodev_control_api_invalid_permissions_response` by design;
- the same stale Router is why **every agent detail page** fails closed, and this was diagnosed rather than assumed. `/agents/orchestrator` and its siblings return HTTP 200 carrying only the `ResourceUnavailable` shell with `autodev_control_api_invalid_agent_detail_response`. Querying the running Router directly with the service credential shows it serves `schema: "autodev-control-agent-detail-v1"`, while `runtime/src/control-api/index.ts` emits `"autodev-control-agent-detail-v2"`, `core/src/control-api/types.ts` declares v2, `tests/router/control-api.test.ts` asserts v2 and passes 27/27, and the Console requires v2. Every other field in the Router's v1 payload satisfies the Console's validator, so the schema string is the whole difference: the running process predates the v2 change. This is environmental, not a Console defect, and the Console is behaving as designed by failing closed rather than rendering a partial agent. Both halves of the contract were then exercised against a throwaway stub serving the exact v2 shape the Runtime source emits — the v2 payload renders the full detail page with no overflow and one `h1`, and the same payload with only the schema flipped to v1 renders the failure shell while leaking neither the agent name nor its `Configured` status. That stub was written to a throwaway directory outside the repository and is not part of the tree; the sandbox this ran in refused its deletion, so it should be removed by hand;
- remote deployment acceptance remains open;
- deployed authenticated receiver **live + graceful-drain/shutdown** acceptance remains open;
- local p25 health, Memory route, authenticated OTLP persistence, Usage filters, and service-token redaction probes pass;
- GitHub read-only Actions runtime state and bounded statistics suites pass across Data, Runtime, and Console; live local Actions data and dev/staged-production browser checks pass, while remote production-release and production-credential acceptance remain open. Dispatch/cancel/rerun/schedule mutations remain unimplemented;
- isolated Prompt edit acceptance used a temporary repository/home with the real pinned Rulesync executable: an operator `PATCH /control/prompts/dry` updated the canonical Markdown, generated/applied `$CODEX_HOME/prompts/dry.md`, returned the new revision with restart-required state, rejected a stale revision with HTTP 409, denied a viewer with HTTP 403, and did not include source text in audit events; headless Chromium submitted the Console form, followed the 303, and reloaded the updated canonical source without client errors. The real repository and user Codex home were not modified by this probe;
- OpenLIT p24-p25 patch application/build checks pass; p26 trace-detail source applies to p25 and its patched-client typecheck plus focused route/middleware tests pass; an isolated p26 validation image builds successfully, while the active image remains p25 and activation/live trace acceptance remain open;
- focused CronLog/Pricing/Evaluation suites pass 166/166; Usage-variable/API-route suites pass 11/11;
- p25 patch-application suite passes 6/6; the current 26-patch OpenLIT source set also applies to pinned OpenLIT 2.1.0; patched p25 client typecheck passes;
- the prompt detail surface now shows the reconciliation the Runtime already computes: `/control/prompts/:name` returns a v4 payload whose `reconciliation` (verdict, desired/observed generations, last apply/observation, last error, bounded operation history) the Console validated but discarded when mapping to `PromptDocument`. `PromptDetailView` renders it through a shared `ReconciliationPanel`, and the convergence badge that Providers used for role toggles moved out of `provider-status.ts` into `components/status/ConvergenceBadge.ts` because desired-vs-actual state is not provider-specific. Verified in Chromium against the live Control API: `/prompts/dry` renders `pending` with both generations and `Not observed` for the fields the Runtime has not seen; `/prompts/orchestrator` renders `not-observed` rather than a synthesized success;
- the transitional external Memory bridge is retired: the Console Memory tab set is Durable Records / Experiences / Outcome Cohorts, the portal tab, `memory-portal.ts`, `MemoryPortalCard`, and the `AUTODEV_OPENLIT_UI_URL` launcher pass-through are deleted, and the launcher now allowlists the two URL variables the Console server reads;
- model enablement now carries the same desired-vs-actual contract as a provider role. It was the only mutable Control API resource with none: `ControlApiModelRecord.enablement` had no convergence field, `patchModel` published no reconciliation at all, and an operator toggling a model got no answer to "did my change land?" while toggling a provider role did. `modelsView` now projects a `ReconciliationStatus` per model and `patchModel` returns the same `ReconciliationView` (verdict, generations, bounded history) the role patch does, which also moves model applies' generations into the audit envelope. The Console guard was renamed `isRoleConvergence` -> `isEnablementWithConvergence` because the contract now serves both resources, and `ModelDetailView` renders the verdict next to the toggle so "the model is enabled" and "we have observed that enablement converge" stay separate statements. Verified in Chromium at 1440 against a stub serving the new contract: `/providers/claude/models/sonnet` renders `Not observed` next to `Disabled`, `/providers/codex/models/gpt-6-luna` renders `pending` next to `Enabled` with the desired generation on its hover title, and against the pre-change shape the guard fails closed with `autodev_control_api_invalid_models_response` rather than rendering an unevidenced model;
- the shared table's width floor is now derived from each table's own declared weights instead of one `min-w-[68rem]` constant, which is what the target-state width rule already specified ("a minimum width equal to the widest declared weight total"). The global constant was fitted to the two widest tables (MCPs 1088 units, Agents 1087) and over-served everything else: the four-column Models table declared 658 units but was held to 1088px, so at 1440 it rendered a 12px horizontal scrollbar for twelve pixels of nothing. Measured after the change at 1440: Models floor 658px with a 1076px container and zero scroll, Providers floor 999px still scrolling its own region at 1024 with zero clipped headers and zero document overflow;
- runtime state is now a real Console surface instead of two dropped fields. `/control/runtime` publishes lifecycle (state, draining, changedAt, active response requests) and the same concurrency projection `/control/routing` carries, but `ControlApiRuntimeResponse.concurrency` was declared as `{ limit, active } & ControlApiConcurrencyStatus` — fields the Runtime has never emitted. `AgentsView` read exactly those two, so the branches could never fire and the panel fell through to a hardcoded `0` for active threads, active sessions, and total denials while the real evidence (`effectivePerSessionLimit`, `activeSubagentThreads`, `activeSessions`, `denials`, `lastDenial`) sat unread in the same response. `fetchRuntime` also had no response guard at all, unlike every other fetch in the file, so any shape rendered as a healthy runtime. Core now declares the real concurrency projection, `fetchRuntime` validates schema/lifecycle/concurrency/counters and fails closed with `autodev_control_api_invalid_runtime_response`, and the panel reads only `/control/runtime` (the Agents page's now-dead `/control/routing` fetch and the view's `routing` prop are removed rather than left as a second copy that could disagree). Absent counters render `Not observed` through one `observed()` helper; a measured zero still renders `0`. Verified in Chromium at 1440: with real evidence the panel shows limit 8, threads 3, sessions 2, denials 17, `per_session_limit`, and a distinct `Draining` badge; with the counters absent it shows `Not observed` for all four while in-flight requests still read `0`;
- every Control API read the Console performs now fails closed on an unreadable response. Nineteen fetches in `console/src/lib/server/control-api.ts` returned their payload unvalidated, so a Runtime whose envelope drifted reached the view as an empty collection or an empty field — and an empty collection is a claim ("no agents are configured", "no MCP servers are configured", "this durable claim has no history") that a shape the Console cannot read does not support. Each fetch now validates the envelope it actually renders and reports the failure: Agents, Memory collections, Memory detail (record/history/experience), the workspace catalog, MCPs, Tools, Hooks, Evaluations, GitHub, Routing, and Runtime each carry their own guard and code. Two distinctions are preserved rather than flattened: a well-formed but empty collection still renders as an observed empty state, and an `unavailable` workspace catalog keeps its own status. Tools' `coverage`/`validity` vocabulary is checked exactly rather than coerced, because those two fields are the page's entire honesty budget. Verified in Chromium: a drifted Agents payload renders `autodev_control_api_invalid_agents_response`, a drifted Memory collection renders `autodev_control_api_invalid_memory_response`, and a valid record with an unreadable history renders the page's own scoped failure rather than an empty timeline or a whole-page 500. Two response guards were added after the Runtime projection itself was checked field by field — the `concurrency.limit`/`active` fiction and an incomplete GitHub fixture were both caught this way, in opposite directions;
- the envelope guards were only half the contract: every catalog row guard checked the row's _identifier_ and nothing else, while the views read several required members off each row. An incomplete row therefore arrived as `ok` and threw during render — an HTTP 500 with no `<h1>` at all, which is strictly worse than the visible failure shell the guards exist to produce. Each collection now has a named row guard covering every required member of its Core type (`isMcpServerRow`, `isToolCatalogRow`, `isGithubWorkflowRow`, `isEvaluationRow`, `isProviderHealth`), matching the discipline `isAgentRecord` already documented. Two of the four would have crashed (`transport.toUpperCase()`, `tool.exposedRoles.includes`, `workflow.schedules.length`); the other two would have _synthesized_ — a missing `enabled`/`declared` compares unequal to `null`/`false` and so reports "Canonical"/"Configured", and a missing `passed` compares as a failure against an evaluation verdict whose real unobserved state is `null`. Both are the failure the target state forbids outright. Two existing fixtures in "Catalog collections fail closed on unreadable responses" had encoded the buggy behaviour as `ok`, which is where the defect survived: the test asserted that a row missing only its identifier was acceptable;
- a guard that is too strict is indistinguishable in the UI from bad data, and it is the failure mode a test suite cannot see. `targetOverrides` is a list of records (`{ target, enabled }`), not a list of strings, so the `isStringList(server.targetOverrides)` check rejected _every_ well-formed MCP catalog and `/mcps` rendered the failure shell with `autodev_control_api_invalid_catalog_response`. The regression fixture for that field now carries a real entry rather than an empty list, because an empty list passes a string-list check and would not have caught it. Found only by running the browser sweep against corrected stub payloads — the stub had been quietly serving incomplete rows the whole time, which is also why five of thirteen routes had no real rendering coverage at all;
- nullable is not the same as absent, and the difference is one character wide. `cooldown` and `lastFailure` are nullable, so `health.cooldown !== null` is the natural test — but a payload that omits the key yields `undefined`, which is not `null`, so the readiness badge read `cooldown.failureClass` off `undefined` and `/providers` returned 500 in every viewport. The provider health guard now distinguishes observed from absent. Sweep after both fixes: 130 measurements (10 widths x 13 routes), 12 of 13 routes rendering real content, every route and width passing; the one route still unexercised is `/usage`, which needs a live OpenLIT instance;
- **the seven detail routes had never been swept.** They are half the product's pages, and every finding above came from the list routes alone. Swept against the live router at 390/768/1280/1536 with real identifiers: layout is clean across all of them, and the reconciliation panel was not. Its labelled facts were laid out `sm:grid-cols-2`, splitting the row evenly, so "Desired generation" rendered in about a third of its half while ~300px sat unused beside every label — and the 64-character generation hash, the one value on that panel worth comparing against its neighbour, was pushed onto two lines. Showing two generations so they can be compared and then wrapping both defeats the reason they share a panel. `sm:grid-cols-[max-content_1fr]` is the shape a definition list wants; both hashes now fit on one line and the panel is ~100px shorter. Guarded, and verified by reverting to `sm:grid-cols-2` and confirming the assertion fails. Two detail routes render the failure shell — `/agents/[id]` and `/providers/[id]/models/[model]` — and both are the same stale-process artifact as `/permissions`, not separate Console bugs: the running router serves `autodev-control-agent-detail-v1` where the Console requires v2, and omits `convergence` from a model enablement where the guard requires it. The current runtime source emits both, so **one router restart clears all three**;
- three columns cut a value with no way to get it back, and all three are invisible to the header-width check because their headers are short ("Type", "State"). They are _content_-width problems. The Prompts TYPE column rendered its badge as "Comman" on every one of the 63 command rows — a `StatusBadge` is the widest thing in that column by a wide margin, and the column declared weight 96. The Skills STATE column declared no weight at all, so it took the 100-unit default and clipped "Configured" at its last glyph. The existing truncation guard did not catch them because `truncatingCellTitle` only titles a cell whose content is a _plain string_: these wrap the value in a `<span>` or a pill for typography, so the cell got no title — and unlike a `Chip` or a link, a bare span recovers nothing. The agent's primary model, the workspace slug, and the Tools source pill now title themselves the way `Chip` does. Measured against the live router: three unrecoverable truncations, then none. **A broader mechanical guard for this class was prototyped and deliberately not shipped** — "a value-ish leaf with no title" flags 31 sites, almost all short labels in wrapping `tokens`/`prose` columns and links that recover through their `href`; a guard that is 90% false positives is not a guard, so the durable protection stays the browser measurement. The Providers credential column still truncates "Missing <ENV_VAR>" by a lot and is left alone: documented as intended, with the full name on the badge's hover title;
- **the fix above patched three symptoms and left the hole open.** The per-view "title it yourself" workaround was applied to the three cells a sweep had happened to catch, while `truncatingCellTitle` still refused to title anything that was not a plain string — and its stated reason, that "a chip titles itself and a link holds the value in its destination", was false for most of the cells it covered. Re-swept with the check corrected to look for a recovery _anywhere inside_ the cell rather than only on an ancestor, and rather than only at one width, 107 unrecoverable cuts remained across six widths: the GitHub cron column is plain spans, the trigger-events column is a `div` of chips, the Tools EDIT column is styled links, and the Prompts name and type columns are a link and a badge. Four of those columns could not be fixed at any width — Tools EDIT needed 191px in the 112 its weight granted, cutting all 25 rows on every viewport including 1280 — so they now wrap instead of truncating, and the other cuts were the same `truncate` default misapplied to a value that is a chip list, a sentence, or the row's own identity. The component now reads the text out of the node tree, so the rule holds for every cell rather than for the cells that happened to be simple, and the test that asserted an element cell must have _no_ title — the bug, encoded as a requirement — now asserts the rule against the three shapes that were actually cut. Proven to fail by restoring the string-only rule. Measured over 19 routes x 6 widths: **859 cut cells with 107 unrecoverable before, 624 cut cells with 0 unrecoverable after**;
- **the one irreversible action in the Console lost its subject on every outcome.** The target state's cross-feature clause names "destructive-action confirmation patterns", and purge is the only irreversible action there is, so it was checked end to end rather than by reading. The confirmation pattern itself is right — a bounded reason code the Runtime accepts, a server-enforced `confirm` field rather than a UI-only guard (purge remains a server-enforced form action, so an unticked box is a request the route refuses), a destructive button variant, and the irreversibility stated twice. But the redirect back to Memory re-selects what was acted on by putting the identifier in the query, and the key that carries it is decided by which tab is being returned to: the experiences tab reads `experienceId`, the records tab reads `recordId`. **Both outcomes spelled it `recordId` regardless**, and a purge's identifier is an _experience_ id — so the redirect landed on the right tab, carrying the right value, under a key that tab ignores. Nothing about it looks wrong: the drawer simply did not open. Verified in Chromium rather than assumed: `?tab=experiences&experienceId=exp-0001` opens the drawer and `?tab=experiences&recordId=exp-0001` does not. The refusal path passed no identifier at all, so nothing on the page said which row had been refused. Both paths now share one `selectionQuery` helper so they cannot disagree, and the JSON success response no longer reports `recordId: payload.recordId`, which answers `""` for a purge — the non-browser caller that had just erased an envelope was told which _record_ it was, which is none. **Two existing fixtures asserted the old redirect strings exactly**, the same shape of fixture that has encoded four of this project's bugs;
- **the shared failure notice was withholding a fact the route already knew.** `ControlFailureNotice` documents why its primary sentence is outcome-free — "the refreshed value it redirects to is the authoritative answer, so the notice must not invent a more specific outcome" — and that reasoning is right. But _must not invent_ is not _must withhold a known fact_. A purge refused because the confirmation box was unticked, and one the Runtime turned down because durable memory still cites the envelope, are opposite situations with opposite next moves; told only "could not be confirmed", the first operator retries the byte-identical request. The route now carries a bounded **code** in the redirect — never a message, so nothing reflects text into the page and nothing can drift from what the route meant by it — and the notice grows one line only when a code is present. Every other mutation surface renders exactly the notice it always did, so the shared pattern is unchanged, and an unrecognised code falls back to the shared sentence rather than inventing a cause. The reason comes from **which check stopped the request, not which action was attempted**: that distinction is invisible in a bare `null` return but not to the operator, because a purge whose reason code the Runtime rejects is _not_ a missing confirmation. `executeAction` therefore returns the reason it refused for, and the first attempt — keying the reason off the action — was caught by its own test before it shipped. The repo's dependency boundaries caught the rest and were right to: a feature may not import `lib`, so the refusal type is derived from the component the view already renders rather than imported across the boundary;
- **the page-rhythm guard could not see the two pages that had actually bypassed it.** The target state asks for "the same status vocabulary, icon sizing, spacing, table density, dialog behavior, and destructive-action confirmation patterns across features", so all four were measured in a browser across 20 routes rather than assumed. Two were already correct and are now evidence rather than hope: every rendered icon is `16x16` in a control or `12x12` as control chrome — the one documented exception — stroke-width is `2px` on every route, and **all 13 tables share one density exactly** (`th 16/10` at `12px/15`, `td 16/12` at `14px/20`). Spacing was not: `/memory` stacked its sections at `gap-8` and the prompt detail page at `gap-5`, where the other twenty pages resolve to `gap-6`, so two pages read as a different product at every width. The cause was not two wrong constants but a **bypass** — `MemoryView` and `PromptDetailView` do not use `PageBody`, they hand-roll the page stack. The guard that should have caught it matched only the exact literal `flex flex-col gap-6`, on the stated ground that "the shared constant and any other gap value are fine", and the two offenders were on `gap-8` and `gap-5`. **The guard's own comment encoded the defect as policy.** The reliable signal in source is not the gap value but the hook: `data-feature` is a page body's identity and only `PageBody` renders it, so a view writing `data-feature` beside its own className has hand-rolled a page body whatever gap it chose — and inner stacks carry no hook, so the guard does not have to guess from a gap value and does not flag panels that legitimately stack at `gap-1` or `gap-2`. Both pages render through `PageBody` now, the prompt detail page keeping its `article` element through the existing `as` prop. **Measured: all 19 pages that render a body resolve to 24px, from 32px and 20px**, verified at 390/768/1280 with content, tables, cards and the memory evidence attributes unchanged. Guard proven to fire by planting the exact bypass that shipped;
- **two routes had never rendered, and every sweep had been counting them as clean.** `/memory` and `/evaluations` need a Memory backend and ClickHouse respectively, and the live router has neither, so both render a failure panel. That is the correct behaviour — and it means every "no findings" result for those routes was clean _because there was nothing there to find a defect in_. A page that renders nothing cannot fail a layout check, so the sweep was measuring absence and reporting it as quality. Two routes plus the seven detail routes is a third of the product measured this way. Pointing a Console at a stub that serves Memory and Evaluations from fixtures and proxies the rest to the live router gave those pages their first rendering coverage — three tabs, 11 cohort rows, 12 stat cards, and the only `columns: 5` ladder rung in the product — and it found **five defects that had been invisible for the whole project**;
- **the container-only guard defect, one level down again, and this time it was live.** `isMemoryExperienceRow` never mentioned `trajectory`, Core declares `ExperienceEnvelope.trajectory` required, and `MemoryExperiencesView` reads `experience.trajectory.format` unguarded — so an envelope well-formed except for one absent field reached the render and threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'format')`, an HTTP 500 with no `<h1>` on the experience detail route. `isMemoryRecordRow` had the same shape one level over: `provenance` and `validity` were checked with `isRecord`, which passes for `{}`, while the view calls `.map` on `provenance.evidence` and reads `validity.state` three times — including a three-way colour choice, so an absent state would also have been coloured as a warning about a claim nobody checked. Three detail and history guards repeated the container check instead of reusing the row guard, so a record that failed closed on the list passed on its own detail page; all three now reuse it. `fetchMemoryUseCohorts` had **no response guard at all** — how nineteen other fetches were hardened earlier and this one was missed — and `isSessionOutcomeCohortPage` validated its envelope and not one cell, while the view calls `.toLocaleString()` on every cell's counts. `outcomeKind` and `useKind` are checked as "string or null" rather than required, because Core defines a null there as "no report exists", which the view renders as unobserved rather than as a failure — flattening that would have made a real state indistinguishable from malformed data. **Two existing fixtures had encoded the bug**: the memory detail and history tests asserted `{ memory: { id: "r1" } }` was `ok`, the identifier-only payload the guards were originally written around. They now carry what the view reads, and assert the old shape is rejected;
- **three heading levels, disagreeing with each other, on the one page nobody had rendered.** The cohorts tab ran `h1` to `h3`; the record and experience detail panels ran `h2` to `h4`, skipping a level; and each of the three Memory views disagreed with the other two. Every other detail route is `h1`, then `h2` from `EntityTitle`, then `h3` for sections. Detail panels are now `h3` and the cohorts tab is `h2`, which is the level each one actually occupies;
- **a drawer title squeezed out of existence by its own badges.** At 390px the experience drawer title measured **zero pixels wide and 224px tall**: nothing painted, and the panel reserved the height of a name it was not showing. The cause is a flex negotiation, and it is worth stating precisely because the two halves of the existing fix are what created it. Badges are `whitespace-nowrap` pills, so their automatic minimum size is their full width and they cannot shrink at all. The title carries `min-w-0` _precisely so a long unbreakable id can shrink and wrap_ — which made the title the only item on the line that **could** give. At a 194px row, "Role: orchestrator" (148px) and "not_run" (79px) plus a 12px gap took everything. The row wraps now, so the badges take their own line and the name keeps whatever line it is on; the chips keep `whitespace-nowrap`, because a badge that breaks mid-word to avoid this trades one defect for another. Measured before and after on the real page: `0x224` to `96x28`, with all five drawer routes at 390/640/1280 keeping real width. Guarded;
- **the `DetailGrid` column ladder, which its own doc called unverified, is now verified.** `DetailGrid.ts` documents the ladder as "arithmetic on declared classes rather than a measurement: these widths have not been confirmed in a browser". Measured over 19 routes at 10 widths, every `columns: 2`, `3` and `4` row lays out exactly where the table says, with no card value overflowing its own card, no title wrapping to three lines, and no card scrolling horizontally. The `5` rung could not be checked on the live router at all, because its only caller is the cohorts tab — and it checks out there too, at five cards only from `xl`;
- **the sweep now reports each route's render state, because "clean" that includes a route which rendered nothing is the same mistake as a check that cannot fail.** The first version of that fix had its own false positive: it inferred "empty" from component counts, and three detail routes that build their layout from `<section>` and plain definition lists — no table, no `data-detail-grid` — were reported as empty while rendering a full page. Rendered-text volume is the honest proxy. Both failures are recorded because the sweep is the durable instrument here: a sweep that reports cleanliness it has not earned is worse than no sweep, since it is evidence. **Final state: 240 measurements, 24 routes × 10 widths, zero findings, 19 routes rendering the product** — against 14 of 22 routes genuinely rendering before;
- **the Console had three words for "we have no evidence", and one page used two of them side by side.** `NOT_OBSERVED_LABEL` exists for exactly this and its own doc comment names the failure it prevents — "a view can say 'Unknown' or 'Unavailable' beside a badge that says 'Not observed', and the page then appears to contradict itself about whether evidence is missing or actively wrong". Eight sites spelled the same state as `Unknown`, one as `N/A`, and one as an em-dash. The visible symptom was `/mcps` rendering two stat cards about the same missing runtime probe: "Active Shims" read `Not observed` and "Health", directly beside it, read `Unknown`, so an operator could not tell whether the Console disagreed with itself or the probe had answered two different questions. Several `StatusBadge`s carried the same split internally — `status: "not-observed"` with `label: "Unknown"`. A second layer made the constant decorative: eighteen more sites hard-coded the _correct_ word as a bare literal, so editing the constant would have moved its twenty-four referents and left the literals behind. All of it now renders the constant, and the one judgement call is recorded in the diff: the em-dash on a workflow run's branch read as a value rather than as an absence, and GitHub reporting no branch is exactly the not-observed case. The guard scans `src` and `app` for those three literals on code lines only, so a comment quoting the word stays legal, and asserts the rendered `/mcps` page carries the canonical word and not the drifted one — **scoped to the three literals deliberately, because "a string that means missing" cannot be told from data by reading source, and a guard that flags 90% false positives is not a guard**;
- **two controls claimed more than they knew, and both were found by measuring all twenty routes rather than by reading views.** Across the whole Console there are exactly four disabled controls, all on `/usage`, and none stated a reason; the target state requires an unobserved control to stay in place, disabled, "with the reason available". Their visible label already read `Not observed`, so every site looked finished — which is why the reason is now its own prop on `SelectField` rather than a convention, rendered twice to the two audiences that need it (a `title` for a pointer, an `aria-describedby` target for a screen reader, and deliberately not `aria-label`, which would replace the visible "Workspace:" label rather than add to it). And `StatCard` decided "is this unobserved" with `value === NOT_OBSERVED_LABEL`, which missed the `/usage` token card: it composes input and output into one value, so with neither reported it read `Not observed / Not observed` and — because neither half equals the label alone — kept `text-2xl` bold. The row therefore showed its one confident measurement directly beside three correctly quiet ones. The test now asks the question the card is actually asking, whether _any_ part is a measurement, so a half-observed composite containing a measured `0` still gets the value scale rather than being understated in the other direction;
- **the truncation rule had the same blind spot one level down, and the cell was clipped as well.** Reading text out of a node tree covered spans, chip rows and links but not `StatusBadge`, which is written with its visible text in a `label` prop: children was empty, the flattening returned `""`, and the cell got no title — the identical hole, one level deeper, found by the sweep reporting three cells whose entire content was the word "Not observed" and which had no recovery. `label` is read specifically rather than by scanning every prop: it is the Console's one convention for "this is the text I show", it is what `StatusBadge` and `Chip` both use for it, and a general scan would eventually describe a cell with its own `title` or `href` instead of its value. Those same three cells were additionally **clipped**: `/mcps` "Default State" is the longest header in its table and fitted comfortably at 152, but the column holds a badge whose longest label needs 117px against the 109px it was granted, so every not-observed server lost 8px off its pill at every viewport up to 768. The header was never the problem, which is precisely why no header-width check finds this class — it is the third instance of the same lesson (Prompts TYPE, Skills STATE, Tools EDIT), and the sweep measures cell content against the column's own box for exactly that reason;
- **two of the new checks were wrong in a way that would have been acted on.** The sweep reported "no `<h1>` on any page at 390px", which is impossible-looking enough to have been fixed without checking; the cause was `hs.filter((h) => h.tag === "h1")` reading `.tag` off a _DOM element_, which is always `undefined`, so the count was zero on every page at every width. The same sweep reported a focus-ring failure on the `/usage` date inputs: `:focus-visible` does not engage for a programmatic `.focus()` on a date input in headless Chromium, so the element genuinely had no ring _as measured_ while having one under a real Tab press. Walking four routes with 157 real Tab stops found zero without a ring. A third, the same run's truncation report, attributed every finding to column 1 because it read the table's first `th` instead of the cell's `cellIndex` — which is why the Tools EDIT column was reported as "Provider role exposure" under the header "Tool". The heading outlines themselves are sound on all 19 routes (no skipped levels, one `h1` each); what the outline does show is that the sidebar's section labels are `h2`s appearing before the page `h1` in DOM order, which is why every route reads `[2,2,2,1,...]`;
- the guard defect repeats one level down: a check that verifies a _container_ without verifying its members is the same failure as one that checks only a row's identifier. Three survived. The permissions policy was `isRecord(value.policy)` and nothing else, so a policy with no members produced four wrong cards in one row — `approvalPolicy` drew nothing at all (React renders no element for `undefined`, so the card was simply blank) while `networkAccess ? "Allowed" : "Blocked"` and `webSearch ? "Enabled" : "Disabled"` read `undefined` as `false` and stated two confident claims the Runtime never made. The GitHub stats projection was `isRecord(stats)`, so an empty record published `NaN%` and an empty stat card. And the paged Memory guard validated the envelope while never touching the items, so a record with no `scope` threw in `formatScopeString` and `/memory` returned 500 with no `<h1>`; `MemoryScope` is a union discriminated on `kind`, so each arm is now checked against the members its own arm declares, since checking only that `kind` is a string would let `kind: "workspace"` with no `workspaceId` render `undefined` as a scope. These are harder to see than a crash because each produces a plausible-looking page rather than an error;
- **the stricter guards were checked against the real Runtime, not only a stub.** Pointing a Console at the live router on `127.0.0.1:4100` (service token from `console/.env.local`, `x-autodev-actor` set to the canonical `LOCAL_CONTROL_API_ACTOR` — both are required, and omitting the actor yields `autodev_control_api_actor_missing`) renders `/agents`, `/providers`, `/github`, `/skills`, `/mcps` and `/tools` against real data: eight agents with their real provider projections and skill/MCP counts, and the stat row correctly distinguishing `Not observed` from a measured `0`. `/permissions` fails closed with `autodev_control_api_invalid_permissions_response`, and the cause is on the Runtime side: the running router (pid 4175, started 13:22) emits `rolePermissions` entries carrying only `readOnly, sandbox, networkAccess, approvals`, with no `mcp` and no `skills`. Core declares both as required and comments that the capability matrix is "one authoritative join rather than a value the Console has to guess", and the current `runtime/src/control-api/index.ts` does emit them — so the process is serving a pre-change build. This predates the guards in this entry: the `mcp`/`skills` requirement was already there, and failing closed is the correct behaviour, because the alternative was a plausible table of eight roles each claiming no MCP servers and no skills. **Restarting the router is still open**, and was deliberately not done here because other agents share that process for their own model calls; `pnpm autodev -- router ensure` is the sanctioned entry point;
- two cells painted _outside_ their own column rather than wrapping or truncating, which is worse than either because the overflow lands on the neighbour. `tokens` cells were `break-normal`, on the stated intent of "wrap between items, never split a token" — but these columns hold identifiers and repository paths, which have no spaces at all, so `break-normal` did not truncate them either: at 390px the GitHub workflow path overran its column by 511px and ran underneath the trigger chips. `break-words` is the semantics that was actually wanted, and headers keep `break-normal` because a header is a label and splitting a label reads as a rendering fault. The Providers role row is a flex line holding a fixed 80px label and a `whitespace-nowrap` toggle badge, so it has a minimum intrinsic width that no wrapping inside the cell can reduce; `flex-wrap` on the line is what keeps that honest. The sweep now measures both classes — headers whose widest word exceeds their content box, and cells whose `scrollWidth` exceeds `clientWidth` under a computed `overflow-x: visible` — because neither is visible in a markup assertion;
- the Otter/chat/docs/onboarding removal was repaired before anything shipped on top of it. Patch 27 removed those surfaces by deleting line ranges, and in five files the deletion straddled a statement boundary and left the remainder: `utils/breadcrumbs.ts` lost its closing bracket, `api-keys/api-reference.tsx` lost a function header, `observability/trace-governance-panel.tsx` lost the evidence/span-reference block and kept an orphan Otter-merged paragraph, `agents/no-coding-agents.tsx` kept an empty `<p>`, and `dashboard/costs/number-stats.tsx` kept a dangling `<StatCard>`. The client did not parse, so the patched image could not have built. Two further files lost declarations without a parse error: the message catalogue lost ~90 constants that retained governance, telemetry, and connector code still calls, and the `openground`, `prompt-hub`, and `vault` pages still imported the deleted getting-started panels. The patch was regenerated against a committed 01-26 baseline, because regenerating it against the pinned commit produced hunks that reverted part of the branding patch; the `middleware.ts`/`sidebar.tsx` hunks are held at their post-27 content so patch 28 still applies on top. Acceptance: all 28 patches apply cleanly to pinned commit `9938c666` from a pristine checkout, the result is byte-identical to the patched tree that typechecks clean, and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors;
- OpenGround is removed rather than left reachable, and removing it exposed three pieces that did not actually belong to it. The `/api/openground/providers` and `/api/openground/models` routes are a CRUD wrapper over `lib/platform/providers` and are the data source for Manage Models and the evaluations model picker, so they moved to `/api/providers`; the provider/model metadata types lived in `types/openground.ts` because OpenGround defined them first, so they moved to `types/providers.ts`; and the four model-management components Manage Models imports moved to `components/(playground)/models`. Deleting the product then removed the rest: routes, API, metrics endpoints, store slice and selectors, ClickHouse tables, analytics events, sidebar/breadcrumb/middleware entries, the OpenPlait read-feature entry, and the cost bucket it contributed to the company-wide rollup. The create migration was replaced by a drop migration so stale deployments are cleaned up and fresh installs never create the tables, following the `drop-vcs-migration` precedent. The same pass dropped the empty `DOCUMENTATION_LINKS` placeholder left behind by the docs removal, the orphaned OpenGround provider-config API, and the API-reference `Controller` group and `controller-poll` branch, which had no endpoints and rendered as dead UI. Acceptance: all 29 patches apply cleanly to pinned commit `9938c666` from a pristine checkout, the resulting client typechecks with zero errors, and 777 client tests pass. The image build could not be re-run here — the container registry is unreachable from this environment, which stalls `docker pull` independently of the patch set;
- the generic dashboard/board authoring product is removed rather than left reachable, and the entry point it owned moved with it. Deleted: the whole `components/(playground)/manage-dashboard/**` tree (board creator, board view, widget renderer, explorer), `app/api/manage-dashboard/**` (board, folder, widget, query, variables CRUD), the `/home`, `/dashboards` and `/d/[id]` routes, and the dashboards store slice, selectors and root-store registration. The library and the schema stay, because the target state requires keeping the chart/widget/query primitives AutoDev Usage needs: `lib/platform/manage-dashboard/widget.ts` still exports `runWidgetQuery`, which `/api/autodev/usage` calls, and the ClickHouse board/widget tables plus `types/manage-dashboard.ts` remain. The dependency runs one way — the library never imports the board creator — so the UI tree could go without dragging the query primitive after it. Two retained things were re-homed rather than deleted or left depending on a deleted module: `formatCompactNumber` moved from `board-creator/utils/formatters` to `lib/format.ts`, because `stat-card` imported it and had no other relationship to the dashboard product; and the coding-agent detail page lost its `overview` tab, which was nothing but the seeded "Coding Agents" board — it now starts on `sessions`, and `coerceTab` is source-aware so a coding agent never lands on a tab it does not have. The per-user drill-down at `/coding-agents/users/[userId]` existed only to embed a board pinned to that user, so it is deleted and `coding_users` drops `getDetailHref`; `getDetailHref` is now optional on the signal config and `signal-list` handles its absence by selecting the row without navigating, which is why the row is no longer a link. `DEFAULT_LOGGED_IN_ROUTE`, the `/` redirect, and the login/register redirects move from `/home` to `/dashboard`, the surviving read-only observability landing — `/dashboard` itself was left alone because it is read-only views over `/api/observability`, not the authoring product. 51 message constants orphaned by this pass are deleted. Acceptance: all 33 patches apply cleanly to pinned commit `9938c666` from a pristine checkout, `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors, and 278 client test suites / 4188 tests pass. Left for a separate change on purpose: `lib/platform/manage-dashboard`'s now-unreachable board CRUD modules (`board`, `board-format`, `folder`, `heirarchy`, `derived-value`, `widget-sql-bridge`) and the board seeds. They are unreachable, but `clickhouse/seed-data/openlit-dashboard-AutoDev-Usage-layout.json` carries a test that enforces a real AutoDev rule — every Usage widget must use a structured query scoped to a single owning `service.name` and none may use raw SQL — so pruning them deserves its own decision rather than riding along with an authoring-product removal;
- the tenancy layer is removed rather than left as a hidden product. Organisations, memberships, invitations, projects, environments, the header's org/project/environment switchers, Settings > Organisation and Projects, the Posthog organisation/project grouping, the context-id chips, and the `x-openlit-organisation-id` / `x-openlit-project-id` / `x-openlit-environment` request headers all went with it, along with two sidebar entries, three breadcrumb trails, fifteen analytics events, the onboarding allowlists, and the rate-limited-route list. What survives is the minimum the retained storage schema still needs: `DatabaseConfig`, `TelemetrySource` and `ConnectorInstance` all carry non-null `organisationId`/`projectId`, so `lib/scope.ts` resolves — and creates, once — a single organisation/project pair and is the only thing that touches it. That is the "singleton rows as hidden implementation detail" case the target state allows, and it is documented as such at the module. `lib/organisation.ts` (~1230 lines, ~20 exported functions covering membership, invitations and project management) is deleted rather than reduced; the retained consumers — `db-config`, `telemetry-source`, `telemetry-source-crud`, `rbac/route`, `api-keys`, coding-agent auth, and the memory connectors — now resolve the singleton directly. Two things collapsed rather than merely unwired: `requireCodingAgentAuth` no longer derives a role from a membership row and its creator-promotion workaround, because the singleton scope creates the caller's membership as owner, so it always returns admin/owner; and `useProjectDatabaseSetup`/`useWorkspaceSetup` became `useDatabaseSetup`, which waits on the datasource list instead of organisation and project loaders. The latter was masking a visible defect — Home's `isSetupLoading` was derived from tenancy loaders, so the page could render a bare filter bar and nothing else. Removing tenancy removes the gate. The header's third control, which was an environment picker backed by the deleted `/api/project/environment` and a per-project `localStorage` key, is now the datasource picker it was always meant to be: the client-selected context that `x-openlit-database-config-id` has always selected server-side. Environment is a constant (`DEFAULT_ENVIRONMENT`) rather than state, because it is what selects which ClickHouse the adapters talk to — a datasource routing concern, not a tenancy one. 110 message constants orphaned by patches 30-32 are deleted, and user-facing copy no longer says "the current project". Acceptance: all 32 patches apply cleanly to pinned commit `9938c666` from a pristine checkout, `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors, and 284 client test suites / 4208 tests pass. Verified against the running client with a local SQLite database and a signed-in session: the header rendered `/ No project / production` before the change and `No datasource selected` after — two of three scope pills gone — and the rendered Home markup contains zero occurrences of "organisation" or "projects". Browser verification of the hydrated shell was not possible in that environment (see the open item above), so the sidebar and Home content were not visually confirmed here;
- the client has one theme, and it was not the one it claimed. Tailwind is configured `darkMode: ["class"]`, but `app/layout.tsx` put the class from a `theme` cookie that only the sidebar toggle ever wrote, so a first-time visitor with no cookie rendered the entire product in light mode — and the sidebar carried a live Appearance Light/Dark switch, which the dark-only contract forbids outright. `<html>` now carries `dark` unconditionally and the body's background no longer depends on a variant. `utils/hooks/useTheme.ts`, `sidebar/theme-switch.tsx` and the Appearance row are deleted, and `next-themes` and `tiny-cookie` are dropped from `package.json` — `tiny-cookie` existed only to persist that preference. Verified in Chromium against the pre-fix markup: the first-visit body painted `rgb(250,250,249)` (stone-50) and now paints `rgb(12,10,9)` (stone-950), with 305 compiled `.dark`-scoped rules in the served stylesheet. A render test asserts the layout's `<html>` class and is verified to fail when `dark` is removed. Once the client could be driven with a real SQLite database and a signed-in session, the whole shell rendered dark and correctly branded AutoDev v2.1.0;
- the 404 page was still a marketing page, and it outlived what it advertised. It rendered an "OpenLIT" wordmark, a nine-card feature grid and confetti — after patch 30 had deleted the Rule Engine, that grid was still pitching `AUTH_FEATURE_RULE_ENGINE`. It was also the one visibly broken page in the app: the container was `bg-white dark:bg-white` and the content column `bg-stone-50` with no dark variant at all, so the right half of the viewport stayed light while the left half went dark. It is now an operator-facing 404 that says the address does not match anything and links to the canonical entry. Verified in Chromium: no `OpenLIT` text, no Rule Engine pitch, zero light-background panels, body `rgb(12,10,9)`. Removing it also orphaned `auth-form.tsx`, `auth-form-container.tsx`, `auto-signin-demo-instance.tsx` (left behind by patch 05, zero consumers) and `common/confetti.tsx`, which are deleted rather than left reachable, plus 73 message constants — 31 `AUTH_*` marketing strings and 23 `RULE_*` strings that survived patch 30's sweep only because this carousel still referenced them;
- **Open and not yet verified:** a static sweep finds 170 light-background `className` values (59 files) with no `dark:` counterpart, which would render light surfaces inside the one dark theme. This has _not_ been fixed, because the sweep cannot distinguish an accidental light surface from an intentional one (code editors, graph canvases, print surfaces), and a blanket rewrite of 170 class strings without rendering each one is exactly the kind of change that looks fixed and is not. It could not be settled by measurement either: the shared browser instance is driven concurrently by other agents, and this sandbox blocks launching a second Chromium (`bootstrap_check_in ... Permission denied`), so a full 21-route rendered sweep is not currently reproducible. Each hit needs an individual render decision;
- the OpenLIT Rule Engine is removed rather than left reachable, and removing it separated one product from another that had been sharing its migration. The rules, rule condition groups, rule conditions, and rule entities tables went with the product via `drop-rule-engine-migration`, following the `drop-vcs-migration` and `drop-openground-migration` precedent, but `openlit_contexts` was created by the same `create-rule-engine-migration` and holds user-authored content, so Context survives and now owns its own `create-context-migration` — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` makes this a no-op for an install that already has the table, so no context rows are lost. Deleting the product then removed the routes, API, components, `lib/platform/rule-engine`, store slice, types, and six test files. Two retained products were coupled to it and are now decoupled rather than left referencing a deleted subsystem. Evaluations no longer enrich results with rule context (the auto-run and offline paths), no longer store `ruleIds`/`contextIds`/`contextApplied` in meta (`OfflineEvaluationResult.contextApplied` became `contexts: { userContextsCount }`), and the evaluation-type config lost the `rules`/`ruleId`/`priority` fields that existed only to feed rule evaluation; the `attributes` SDK option went with them rather than being silently ignored server-side. The governance trace report lost the rule-match dimension: `GovernanceRuleMatch`, `rules`, and `rule_match_count` are gone, `summarizeGovernanceReport` takes two arguments instead of three, and the report's passport fingerprint no longer hashes a rule match. The same sweep removed the plumbing — middleware matchers, sidebar entry, breadcrumbs, token allowlists, 27 analytics events, the `rule_engine_change` alert trigger, `telemetry-snapshot`'s `rules_total`, and the API-reference catalogue group. 353 message constants that patches 27-30 orphaned were deleted with it; the count is measured, not asserted, by comparing each constant's reference count against the pinned upstream checkout. Acceptance: all 30 patches apply cleanly to pinned commit `9938c666` from a pristine checkout, the resulting client typechecks with zero `tsc --noEmit` errors, and all 296 client test suites / 4434 tests pass. The jump from the 777 tests reported for the 29-patch state is not new coverage — it is the first run in which the Prisma-backed suites execute at all: the shared `node_modules` carries an x86_64 query engine while this host runs arm64 node, so every suite touching Prisma aborted the whole jest worker, and passing `PRISMA_QUERY_ENGINE_LIBRARY` at an arm64 engine already on disk restores them. Future runs should use that variable rather than reporting a partial count as a pass. Three defects in the committed chain were repaired on the way, none of them caused by this change: `controller-removal.test.ts` asserted ten Controller-only constants were gone while all ten were still declared, and read a `hi.ts` locale that an earlier patch had already deleted (it now derives the locale list from the directory, so neither failure can recur); `datasource/secret.test.ts` hard-coded "OpenLIT vault" into six `toThrow` patterns and broke on the rebrand, and now asserts against the message constants it is testing; and `helpers/client/user.test.ts` asserted that an app-init profile fetch signs the user out on any error, which the current implementation deliberately does not do, so the test now pins the real contract instead. The image build still cannot be re-run here — the container registry is unreachable from this environment, which stalls `docker pull` independently of the patch set;
- the additive OpenLIT AutoDev pages are deleted rather than hidden. `/autodev` and its MCPs, Providers, Runtime, and Skills pages duplicated Console surfaces, and once the Console runtime panel landed, `/autodev/runtime` had no Console equivalent left either. `28-remove-autodev-pages.patch` deletes the pages, their layout, the five same-origin API proxy routes, the `AutoDev Control` sidebar entry, and the `/autodev` middleware matcher exemptions. `lib/autodev/control-api.ts` is kept, not deleted, because the Memory connector adapter still calls `forwardToControlApi`; only the page-only response types and the two helpers the pages were the sole callers of are removed, so nothing is left exported for a consumer that no longer exists. Verified by applying all 28 patches in order to a pristine checkout of the pinned commit `9938c666`: every patch applies cleanly, the `/autodev` route tree is absent, the sidebar entry and matcher exemptions are gone, `/api/autodev/usage/*` and the memory connector adapter are untouched, and the proxy's token-leak assertions still run. The memory/usage additive patches (`08`-`16`, `22`) remain, since those capabilities are still OpenLIT-owned;
- deleting the board-authoring product left the AutoDev Usage endpoint broken, and the residue was a set of tables nothing wrote to. `runWidgetQuery` resolved its widget from a row in `openlit_widget`, but the seeder that populated those rows was one of the things patch 33 deleted, so every Usage panel resolved no widget, returned `WIDGET_FETCH_FAILED`, and reported `observed: false`. This was a real production break introduced by the previous patch and found only by auditing what the surviving caller actually passes — a green test suite did not catch it, because `route.test.ts` mocks `runWidgetQuery` outright and therefore never saw the id. The runner now takes the `WidgetDefinition` the caller already holds, which also means `optInVariables` and `variableScopeOverrides` are read from the seed rather than a stored copy that had drifted from it. `getWidgetById`, `getWidgets`, `createWidget`, `updateWidget` and `deleteWidget` are deleted, along with the `userQuery` override that only the removed query-run editor supplied and `helpers/server/widget.ts` (the write-side half of a normalisation pair with no remaining writer). `34-remove-board-authoring-tables.patch` also replaces `create-custom-dashboards-migration` and `add-board-variables-column-migration` with `drop-dashboard-authoring-migration`, so an existing install drops `openlit_board`, `openlit_folder`, `openlit_widget` and `openlit_board_widget` instead of carrying them forever, and `dashboards_total` leaves `telemetry-snapshot` — it counted a table with no writer, so it reported a frozen number to PostHog indefinitely, which is the "unreadable ≠ empty" failure in its outbound form. `widget-sql-bridge` had the same failure internally: a period-over-period seed with no previous-period row emitted `previous_count: 0`, and a zero reads as "flat" rather than "not observed", so the previous column is now omitted when the baseline row is absent. Acceptance: all 34 patches apply cleanly to `9938c666` from a pristine checkout, the resulting client typechecks with zero `tsc --noEmit` errors, and 273 suites / 4147 tests pass (down from 278 / 4188, which is exactly the five suites this patch deletes). Both new guards were confirmed able to fail before being trusted: reverting the Usage route to `runWidgetQuery(widgetId, …)` fails the seeded-definition handoff assertion, and re-arming the `if (previousRow)` branch fails the omitted-baseline assertion with `Received value: 0`. `tests/openlit-patches-apply.test.ts` had been asserting on the board-authoring files this patch removes; those assertions now pin the post-removal boundary instead, and the test's four remaining failures are sandbox-only (heredoc and clone restrictions) and reproduce unchanged at `HEAD`;
- the Vault is no longer an administrator-facing credential store, while its read paths stay. `35-remove-vault-administration.patch` deletes the `/vault` page, its `form.tsx`/`header.tsx`, `POST/GET /api/vault` and `/api/vault/[id]`, the sidebar entry, both breadcrumb trails, the `/vault` middleware matchers, the `/api/vault` entries in the token-allowlist and demo-account restriction lists, and the `upsert-secret` API-reference entry. What survives is not admin surface but load-bearing reads: `GET /api/vault/get-secrets` is called by both bundled OpenLIT SDKs (`sdk/python/src/openlit/__init__.py:573`, `sdk/typescript/src/features/vault.ts:16`), `getSecretById` resolves the datasource HTTP secret and the evaluation configuration's judge credential (both store a vault id), and `upsertSecret` keeps exactly one non-admin caller — telemetry-source provisioning, which cannot use it to name an arbitrary secret. `deleteSecret` goes with the admin API because nothing else called it. Two consequences are worth stating plainly rather than hiding. First, a capability regression: the evaluation settings screen could pick or create a judge credential through the list route that is now deleted, so that screen no longer offers the picker and instead says whether a credential is configured and that one cannot be set there — an already-configured credential still round-trips on save. Second, a remaining second-authority path that is deliberately **not** taken here: `POST /api/telemetry-source` still accepts inline `credentials` and persists them to the Vault, so datasource credentials have not yet moved to AutoDev runtime configuration; that needs its own change because both provisioning and `deleteTelemetrySource` depend on the write, and the latter already leaks its secret today, which is pre-existing and out of scope here. Acceptance: all 35 patches apply cleanly to `9938c666`, the resulting client typechecks with zero `tsc --noEmit` errors, 273 suites / 4141 tests pass, and 19 assertions in `tests/openlit-patches-apply.test.ts` pin both the absent admin files and the surviving read paths. That test's patch-name check was rewritten from a per-patch `if` ladder to a data-driven equality — the ladder pushed the callback past the sonarjs complexity ceiling, and asserting the series equals the known names in order is stricter, so an unexpected patch now fails rather than passing silently. The file's four remaining failures are sandbox-only (heredoc and clone restrictions, including an upstream clone that ships without `constants/messages/hi.ts`) and reproduce unchanged at `HEAD`;
- browser verification is working again, and it immediately paid for itself. The Playwright MCP server is enabled but its tools are not exposed to this session, and a bare `chromium.launch()` is sandbox-blocked — which had been recorded as "browser unavailable". That conclusion was wrong and was generalised from one failed launch mode. A standalone launch succeeds with the `chromium_headless_shell-1234` executable plus **both** `--single-process` and `--no-sandbox` (neither flag alone works, and `executablePath` is still required because the installed revisions do not match what the pinned Playwright expects). A loop over flag variants printing the failure per variant found it in one pass; writing the browser off after the first failure would have cost every finding below. Sweeps must record `location.pathname` in the same `evaluate` as the measurement — two routes in the first sweep silently redirected client-side and would otherwise have been reported as the route that was asked for;
- the sidebar's "Browse" button still pushed `/home`, which patch 33 deleted, so primary navigation landed on the 404. Found by clicking it in Chromium, not by reading code; it now routes to `/dashboard`, and the click is verified to land on a page with no "page not found" text. `isActive` had also kept special cases for `/organisation`, `/organisation/projects` and `/dashboards`, all deleted by patches 32-33. Six middleware matcher entries had no page behind them (`/observability`, `/coding-agents`, `/d/:path*`, `/telemetry-enabled` and two `:path*` forms), so auth ran for URLs that always 404; they are removed, and a guard asserts each stays out — confirmed to fail when `/observability` was re-added. Every one of the 12 sidebar destinations now returns 200;
- both applications render dark-only in the browser, which closes the outstanding light-surface sweep. The OpenLIT client serves 16 routes at body `rgb(12,10,9)` and the Console serves 13 routes at `rgb(2,6,23)`. The only light-computed elements are intentional: 1.5px coloured status dots, one accent button, and the white primary CTA on the Memory empty state. The "unreadable ≠ empty" rule is visibly holding — the Console Agents view reports **Not observed** with "No runtime health probe" / "No reconciliation observation" instead of a zero, and Usage shows a banner saying telemetry values remain not observed rather than rendering an empty chart. Screenshots are in `~/.playwright-mcp/shots/`;
- the OpenAPI catalogue and the account profile surface are removed, since the target state names both and neither is AutoDev-owned. `/openapi-spec` documented a third-party SDK's HTTP surface; AutoDev's own API is the Control API, documented in the repository, so the page, the `api-reference` component, the sidebar entry, the "API specification" button on the API-keys header and ten `OPENAPI_SPEC_*` / `INTERACTIVE_API_REFERENCE` constants all go. `/settings/profile` was the account profile / account-scoped preferences page, and AutoDev identity is owned by the runtime. Removing it exposed a second-order bug worth naming: `app/(playground)/settings/page.tsx` redirected to `/settings/profile`, so the entire `/settings` section would have started 404ing. It now redirects to `/settings/api-keys`, verified in Chromium to land on `/settings/api-keys` with an "API Keys" heading and no "page not found" text. The profile tab also leaves the settings tab list and the sidebar. Removing the last consumer of `settings.test.ts`'"'"'s profile tab made that test assert a removed surface, so it was rewritten to pin the surviving tab and to assert the profile path is gone;
- **the Console's own links had never been audited, and the audit needed a second rule to be useful.** `tests/console-internal-links.test.ts` applies the fork's check to the Console's thirteen routes. The string-shape pass (`href`, `redirect`, nav-table entries) found nothing, which looked like a clean result and was not: `canonicalNavPath(section)` is `` `/${section.toLowerCase()}` ``, so the sidebar builds every href from a section name and a shape-based scan cannot see one at all — and the OpenLIT `Agents` 404 was exactly a nav entry with no literal URL. Two more assertions close that. One reads the canonical sections out of `core/src/navigation.ts` and checks `` `/${section.toLowerCase()}` `` against the served routes, so a section without a page fails. One scans every absolute path literal in `src/components`, `src/features` and `app` and requires each to resolve, which catches an href computed through a variable or a ternary — verified by planting `"/usage-typo"` into the nav href, which the shape-based pass missed and the literal pass caught by name. That second rule is scoped away from `src/lib` on purpose: the Console's `control-api.ts` calls the Runtime's `/control/*` endpoints, and those are not Console routes. All thirteen sections resolve and no UI path literal is dead.
- **four dead links got through review before anything automated them, so the link target is now a test.** `/settings/database-config` (a redirect to `/organisation`, deleted in patch 32), `/rule-engine/<id>` (linked from the evaluation panel, deleted in patch 30), `/manage-models` (an alias nothing linked to) and `/agents` (the sidebar entry left behind when patch 37 deleted the agents page) were all reachable by clicking, all dead, and all of the same shape: a page was removed and a reference was not. Reading for them one at a time does not scale, so `tests/openlit-internal-links.test.ts` derives the served route set from the App Router's own `page.tsx`/`route.ts` files and diffs it against every internal target in the source — `href`, `router.push`/`replace`, `window.open`, fetch `url`, `link:` navigation entries, `redirect()`, and `routerRef.replace`. It found `/agents` immediately and then found nothing else, which is the claim worth making. Three false-positive classes had to be designed out first: interpolated segments (`/api/context/${id}`), catch-all routes (`/api/telemetry/[...segments]`), and a literal parent whose only children are parameters (`/evaluations/evaluators/${id}`); matching the interpolated segment against `[id]` reported 11 broken links that all worked. It is proven able to go red — run against the un-patched 01-41 tree it reports exactly `constants/sidebar.tsx (link entry) -> /agents` and nothing else. It skips when no OpenLIT tree is materialised, because "the fork is not checked out here" is not a product defect.
- **the Agents entry was in the sidebar and led to a 404, and the header app resolver hard-coded the same dead route.** Chromium shows `Agents` rendered under "MY APPS" with `/agents` answering 404 "Page not found". Patch 37 removed the page and the `/coding-agents` routes but left both. `getActiveApp` was worse than dead: it mapped any `/coding-agents` pathname onto the Agents app and fell back to a hard-coded `{ title: "Agents", href: "/agents" }` when the sidebar had no such item, so the header could name an app whose own page did not exist. Both are gone, along with four icon imports (`Building2`, `FolderKanban`, `Home`, `User`) that earlier removals had orphaned. Three tests pinned the removed surface — including one asserting the hard-coded fallback — and were replaced with an assertion that `/agents` and `/coding-agents` now resolve to no app. The `/api/coding-agents/**` data plane AutoDev syncs is a different thing and is untouched.
- **the Rule Engine's last UI trace was a list of 404s.** The request evaluation panel still rendered a "Rule Engine & Run Details" section whose "Rules applied" entries linked to `/rule-engine/<id>` — a route patch 30 deleted. The block was fed by a `ruleContext` prop that patch 30 also stopped producing, so it could never populate, and `EvaluationRunCard` accepted the same prop without ever reading it. The panel around it is not rule data, though: it shows the evaluation engine model, manual/auto provenance, and context entity links to `/context/<id>`, which is live. So the rule trace came out and the run details stayed — `EvaluationRunDetails` under a "Run Details" heading, with the `ruleContext` threading gone from the call chain. The assertions pin both halves, so a later cleanup cannot take the live information along with the dead trace.
- **the Manage models tab could not work at all, and it said it was empty.** Four defects stacked, and the browser showed only the outermost one. Five provider/model routes resolved identity with `getServerSession(authOptions)` while their sibling `/api/providers` used `getCurrentUser()`, which carries the single-operator fallback: AutoDev has no login, so those five answered 401 for every operator. The tab then rendered that 401 as **"No models found"** — a confident empty catalog over a read that never happened, which is precisely the failure the target state forbids. Making the failure visible exposed two more behind it: the sidebar had no way to show one, even though `useFetchWrapper` already carried `error` and `isFetched` that the component ignored; and `parseFetchBody` passed a framework error page straight through as the message, so the new honest panel displayed a literal `<!DOCTYPE html>...` document. Separately, two components requested `/api/providers/providers`, a path that has never existed — the route is `/api/providers` — so the evaluations model picker 404'd the same way, and the route's own doc comment named the wrong path, which is what misled both callers. All four are fixed at source: the canonical accessor, a `loadError` branch that cannot fall through to the empty state, an HTML body that never becomes a message, and the correct URL. Chromium now shows **"Model catalog unavailable — No database config present!"** instead of "No models found", and the request is a 500 carrying a true reason rather than a 401.
- **`/manage-models` was a redirect nothing linked to, and its breadcrumb entry was duplicated.** It pointed at `/costs?tab=models`, which is the real destination and still works, so the alias, its middleware matcher entry and its breadcrumb entry were dead weight. Removing that entry revealed the whole `/costs` + `/pricing` block was duplicated verbatim — a leftover from patch 29's OpenGround removal — so the second copy went too, and an assertion now pins the count at exactly one.
- **multi-user database-config sharing is removed, and finding it surfaced a second broken link.** The share affordance was a dialog that invited an email and granted `canEdit`/`canDelete`/`canShare` on a database config — a second-user concept with no second user. Removed: `share-dialog.tsx`, `POST /api/db-config/share`, `shareDBConfig`, `moveSharedDBConfigToDBUser`, the `DatabaseConfigInvitedUser` model and queue, the three grant columns on `DatabaseConfigUser`, the `auth.ts` `events.createUser` hook and `lib/user.ts` call that existed only to claim a shared config, and a Prisma migration that drops the table and columns on existing installs. `checkPermissionForDbAction` went with them: grants exist to constrain _other_ people, so mutating a config is now gated on `requireOwnedDBConfig`, which asks whether the caller's own link to that config exists and refuses otherwise. That guard is mutation-tested — replacing it with a stub turns three db-config tests red — because a permission check that cannot refuse is the same class of defect as a synthesised zero.
- **the organisation RBAC layer was a gate that could not refuse, and it was spread across fifteen routes.** `lib/rbac/current.ts` held three functions: `requireCurrentOrganisationPermission(permission)` returned `null` no matter what it was asked, and `withCurrentOrganisationPermission` / `requireCurrentOrganisationEntitledPermission` returned the handler unchanged. Every caller therefore read as if it were authorising something while authorising nothing. The module is deleted and its 15 route call sites unwrapped (api-key, db-config, evaluation, pricing, prompt, providers). One test asserted the wrapper was called with `"pricing:export"` — a test that pinned the fiction rather than the behaviour — so it was deleted rather than rewritten.
- **`DatabaseConfigTabs` was the share dialog's only host and nothing else rendered it.** Its sole consumer was `/settings/database-config`, which patch 32 had already turned into a redirect. It was dead product code, so it and its test went, taking the now-unused `DatabaseConfigTabItemProps`/`DatabaseConfigTabsProps` types with it.
- **the header datasource pill's only "add a config" link led to a 404, found by clicking it.** "No datasource selected" opens a dropdown whose one write action linked to `/settings/database-config`, and that page redirected to `/organisation` — deleted in patch 32 — so it rendered "Page not found". Confirmed in Chromium: the click lands on `/organisation` with an `<h1>Page not found</h1>`. The link now points at `/connectors?type=clickhouse`, which required the connectors page to actually read `?type=` (its `openType` prop existed and was only ever set by an in-page button that opened whichever connector type happened to sort first). Re-tested in Chromium: the click now lands on `/connectors?type=clickhouse` with the "Add ClickHouse connector" form open and all nine fields rendered. The stale page, its breadcrumb entry and its test are deleted. A 19-route sweep after the change reports HTTP 200 on every real page, no document overflow, and no share affordance in any rendered body; the only 404s left were the four `/telemetry/{traces,metrics,exceptions,logs}` detail segments — and the `logs` one was not a designed absence, which patch 44 corrects below.
- **patch 39 verified as a chain, not as a tree.** All 39 patches apply to `9938c666` in order, the applied result is byte-identical to the tested working tree, `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and the suite is 271 files / 4123 tests. The 21 new assertions in `tests/openlit-patches-apply.test.ts` were run against a deliberately un-patched 01-38 tree first: all 21 go red there and pass on 01-39, so they are evidence rather than decoration.
- **the link guard could not see a link that had no literal href, and three product removals had left exactly that.** `tests/openlit-internal-links.test.ts` matches on the _shape_ of a navigation target (`href=`, `router.push`, `redirect()`), so `href={projectId ? "/organisation/project/${projectId}/connectors" : "/connectors"}` contributed nothing to inspect — and that ternary was the residue patch 32 left behind. `tests/openlit-path-literals.test.ts` scans every absolute path literal in the client instead, deriving the page and API route sets from the App Router's own files. Five exclusions were needed and each one is measured rather than assumed: `[param]` wildcards for API routes (`/api/evaluation/llm/Hallucination` → `/api/evaluation/llm/[evalType]`), a segment-prefix rule for `pathname.startsWith("/api")`, a document-extension rule (`/openlit/${slug(content)}.md`), `utils/validation.ts`, which matches macOS/Linux path roots inside error text, and the regex replacement flags (`"/g,"`). Middleware matchers are deliberately **not** excluded — `"/settings/:path*"` is reduced to `/settings` and matched as a page prefix, which is what makes a stale `"/exceptions"` entry a finding rather than a suppressed one. Against the 01-42 tree it reports 17 dead literals and one ungated page; against 01-44, zero. The scanner is a module, not a test, because `tests/openlit-patches-apply.test.ts` now calls it against the tree it just applied: a guard that only runs when `OPENLIT_CLIENT_DIR` happens to be set is a guard that usually does not run. A second assertion inverts the direction — every page route must appear in `config.matcher`, since a page outside it silently skips the CSRF, auth and demo-account chain.
